# New outbreak of mpox in Anchorage prompts advisory from state health officials

The contagious disease, which was a problem during a global outbreak in 2022, is emerging again around in the nation

![A colorized electron micrograph image shows mpox virus particles, in red and yellow, found within infected cells, colored blue. The virus particles are in various stages of maturity, which accounts for differences in shape. The image also features virus factories, shown in brown, where viruses replicate, mature and assemble. (Image provided by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases/National Institutes of Health)](https://alaskabeacon.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/53601259757_e84fdd0180_o-1536x1201.jpg)

A colorized electron micrograph image shows mpox virus particles, in red and yellow, found within infected cells, colored blue. The virus particles are in various stages of maturity, which accounts for differences in shape. The image also features virus factories, shown in brown, where viruses replicate, mature and assemble. (Image provided by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases/National Institutes of Health)

A rare viral disease has emerged in an outbreak in Alaska’s largest city that appears to be expanding, state health officials report.

There are now four new cases in Anchorage of [mpox](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/22371-monkeypox), a viral disease formerly called monkeypox that is spread through close contact and can be fatal.

None of the patients reported traveling outside the state in month-long period before becoming infected.

It is the highest number of annual mpox cases in Alaska since 2022, when five cases were diagnosed in the state amid a [global outbreak](https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/social-sciences-and-humanities/2022-mpox-outbreak/). Between 2023 and 2025, there were only two Alaska cases.

Three of the Anchorage cases emerged in October and were reported last week through a state Department of Health [alert](https://health.alaska.gov/media/i0ljiz44/akphan_20261029_mpox.pdf) intended to raise awareness in the public and among healthcare providers. “We heard you loud and clear. Arizonans rejected partisan extremism and chose a new direction,” Sundareshan said in a statement. “I am proud of what we accomplished together during my time as minority leader, and I’m ready to lead us into the next chapter.”
